meta.description: For measures the BIS defines the same way in each country: each economy's surprise beside the median surprise of the other Southeast Asian economies.

sources.name: BIS statistics (policy rates, consumer prices, exchange rates, effective exchange rates)
sources.licence: Terms of permitted use of BIS statistics (https://www.bis.org/terms_statistics.htm). Use is unrestricted provided the BIS is cited as the source, the use does not imply endorsement, and inclusion in a commercial product brings no additional charge to users. The statistics are not investment advice. The site cites the BIS under every table.

limitations: Figures are the latest published values and are revised by their publishers. A flag can appear or disappear when a figure is revised.
A flag means a move was large against the series' own last ten years. It does not say why the move happened or what comes next, and it is a research lead, not advice.
With a threshold of 2.5 spreads, roughly one or two readings in a hundred are flagged by chance alone, and more for series with fat tails. The backtest shows how often.
Southeast Asian series come from the BIS, which compiles them from national sources on one definition. Vietnam has only its exchange rate there, and Singapore has no policy rate.
This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.

Source: BIS statistics, FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, from US federal agencies), Department of Statistics Malaysia (OpenDOSM), Indeed Hiring Lab (CC BY 4.0). Surprises, flags and forecasts are this site's calculations, not the publishers'.

finding.label: observation
finding.reason: Measured moves compared with each series' own published history. No model is involved, so a flag says something unusual happened, not why, and not what comes next.
